data: No version is tagged yet. This page is checked against slides --help built from main after go-slides/slides#4 (2026-10-18); anything here may change before the first release. slides [deck.md] [flags] slides [command] [flags] deck.md
data.commands#Commands: Command What it does build writes the presentation as HTML, or as a PDF or images (see below). The default: slides deck.md is slides build deck.md expand prints the deck as plain Marp Markdown: templates expanded, kinds replaced by the directives they stand for notes prints the speaker notes kinds lists the kinds the deck can use and what they set themes lists the themes version prints the version (so does slides --version) completion prints a shell completion script: bash, zsh, fish or powershell slides --help prints the flags of a command. Flags may come before or after the deck: slides deck.md -o out.html and slides -o out.html deck.md are the same. Long flags take two dashes (--html); -o is the only short one. build writes deck.html beside deck.md unless -o says otherwise.
data.flags#Flags: Flag Commands What it does -o, --output file build, expand, notes output file; - for standard output --config file all configuration file; by default slides.yaml next to the deck, if there is one --no-config all do not read a configuration file --theme-set path all a theme CSS file, or a directory of them (repeatable) --kinds file all a YAML file of kinds (repeatable) --data file all a YAML or JSON file of template data (repeatable) --set key=value all one template value (repeatable) --no-template all do not expand Go templates --strict-yaml all parse directives as strict YAML, as plain Marpit does (Marp Core parses them loosely) --html build allow all raw HTML; by default, Marp Core’s allowlist --lang code build the page’s lang when the deck sets none --bare build stack the slides, without the presenting script --pdf build write a PDF, one page per slide, with an outline (also chosen by -o file.pdf) --images png|jpeg build write one image per slide: deck.001.png, … --image png|jpeg build write the first slide as an image (also chosen by -o file.png or -o file.jpg) --jpeg-quality n build JPEG quality, 1 to 100 (default 85)
data.images-and-pdf#Images and PDF:
-o with a .pdf, .png or .jpg extension picks the format, as marp-cli does. Output directories are created. A PDF has one page per slide, at the slide’s size, and an outline of the slides and their headings.
Rendering is done by go-webengine and the PDF is written by go-pdfkit; the fonts the built-in themes ask for (Lato, Roboto Mono) come from go-opentype/fonts and are embedded, so no render touches the network. There is no Chrome.
Known limits, each tracked in the library it belongs to:
Images are rendered at one device pixel per CSS pixel (1280×720 for 16:9), until go-webengine has a device scale factor. Several or split backgrounds (![bg left]) need percentage heights in go-webengine. A single background already renders. Local image files need opt-in file:// loading in go-webengine. data: URIs and http(s) images render now. Headings are lighter than with Lato Black: go-opentype/fonts carries one regular instance of Lato and Roboto Mono, so gaia and uncover headings are not as heavy.
data.planned#Planned: Not built yet: PPTX output, math, code highlighting and emoji. When they arrive, they are commands or flags here.
data.slidesyaml#slides.yaml:
A configuration file next to the deck applies to it, so a folder of decks shares one:
kinds: kinds.yaml # a mapping of kinds, or file(s) holding one themes: # theme CSS files or directories - themes/ data: # template data company: Example Inc. html: false # allow all raw HTML lang: en Kinds: the deck’s own kinds: override the file’s and the command line’s. Data: the file’s and the command line’s data override the deck’s front matter, so one deck can be built with different data.

data.a-first-deck#A first deck:
Any Marp deck is one. Save this as talk.md:
--- marp: true theme: default paginate: true footer: "{{ .talk }}" data: talk: Pure Go slides topics: [Why, How, Next] --- # {{ .talk }} {{ range .topics }} --- # {{ . }} {{ end }} The front matter is Marp’s, plus data:. The body is a Go template: the range writes one slide per topic, each starting with ---, and the first slide is of the built-in kind title (no header, no footer, no page number).
data.build-it#Build it: slides talk.md # writes talk.html beside the deck slides -o slides.html talk.md # or somewhere else; -o - for standard output slides with no command is slides build. Flags may come before or after the deck. Open the HTML in a browser; the keyboard moves between slides.
data.expand-it#Expand it:
slides expand talk.md prints the same deck as plain Marp Markdown (output of main at 4ae5c49, 2026-10-18):
--- marp: true theme: default paginate: true footer: "Pure Go slides" --- # Pure Go slides --- # Why --- # How --- # Next The four slides the range generated, the footer with its value, and the title kind replaced by the spot directives it stands for. Anything that reads Marp — marp-cli, the VS Code extension — can take it from there, so nothing written with go-slides' additions is locked in.
data.export-images-and-pdf#Export images and: slides talk.md --pdf # one page per slide, with an outline slides talk.md --images png # talk.001.png, talk.002.png, … slides talk.md --image jpeg # the first slide only slides talk.md -o out/slides.pdf # the extension picks the format; out/ is created slides talk.md --images jpeg --jpeg-quality 90 No browser is involved: go-webengine renders the slides and go-pdfkit writes the PDF. This is on main with known limits (1× resolution, split backgrounds, local image files); see Command line.
data.install#Install:
No version is tagged yet, so install from main (Go 1.27.2 or later):
go install github.com/go-slides/slides/cmd/slides@main slides is one static Go binary with no cgo: nothing else to install, no Node, no Chrome. With the first release this line becomes @latest.
data.next#Next: Marp compatibility: what is read the way Marp reads it. Templates and Kinds: the two additions. Command line: every command and flag.

data: A kind is a named preset of local directives: header, footer, pagination, class, background. A slide says what it is — title, section — instead of repeating how it looks, and a deck’s look is changed in one place.
data.built-in#Built in: Kind Sets title class: lead, no page number, no header, no footer section class: lead content nothing: the deck’s own defaults blank no page number, no header, no footer Any of them can be redefined.
data.defining-kinds#Defining kinds:
In the front matter:
--- marp: true kinds: chapter: class: invert backgroundColor: "#1e1b4b" paginate: false quote: extends: blank class: quote --- extends starts a kind from another one’s directives. A kind accepts the local directives and extends.
data.leaving-go-slides#Leaving go-slides: slides expand writes every kind out as the spot directives it stands for, slide by slide, so the result is plain Marp Markdown that any Marp tool reads.
data.sharing-kinds#Sharing kinds:
A team’s kinds belong in one file every deck names:
# kinds.yaml chapter: class: invert paginate: false --- marp: true kinds: kinds.yaml # or a list of files --- or --kinds kinds.yaml on the command line, or kinds: in slides.yaml. The order is: the built-in kinds, then the command line and the configuration file, then the deck’s own kinds:.
slides kinds talk.md lists the kinds a deck can use and what each one sets.
data.using-a-kind#Using a kind: # Part two --- ![bg](photo.jpg) kind: applies like a local directive: to this slide and the ones after it. _kind: applies like a spot directive: to this slide only. Switching kinds first clears what the previous kind set, so a class or a footer never leaks from one kind into the next. Directives written on the slide itself win over the kind.

data: A deck written for Marp is a go-slides deck. The rules below are Marpit’s and Marp Core’s; where go-slides differs, this page says so.
data.around-the-slide#Around the slide: Header and footer: header: and footer: directives, in Markdown. Pagination: paginate: true. Speaker notes: an HTML comment that is not a directive is a note. slides notes prints them. Fragmented lists: a list written with * (or 1)) appears item by item, as in Marp.
data.directives#Directives: Kind Where Applies to global front matter, or anywhere the whole deck: theme, style, headingDivider, lang… local this slide and the ones after it spot (underscore) this slide only The local directives are Marpit’s: paginate, header, footer, class, backgroundColor, backgroundImage, backgroundPosition, backgroundRepeat, backgroundSize, color. Directives are parsed as loose YAML, as Marp Core does; --strict-yaml parses them as plain Marpit does.
data.images#Images: ![bg](image.jpg) makes an image the slide’s background, with Marp’s keywords: bg contain, bg cover, bg 50%, bg left/bg right for a split background, several bg images side by side, and the image filters (blur, sepia, grayscale…). Inline image sizes (w:200px, h:) are read as Marp reads them.
data.slides#Slides: A horizontal ruler — --- on a line of its own, as Marpit splits — starts a new slide, and so does a heading of the level the headingDivider directive names. The front matter, between the first two ---, holds global directives and the deck’s data.
data.themes#Themes: default, gaia and uncover are built in, selected with theme:. A theme of your own is a CSS file with Marp’s /* @theme name */ comment, given with --theme-set or listed under themes: in slides.yaml.
data.where-go-slides-differs#Where go-slides: Templates. {{ }} in the body is a Go template action (see Templates). A deck that shows {{ as text outside a code block needs --no-template, or the text escaped as Go templates escape it. Code blocks and code spans are left alone. Kinds. kind: and _kind: are directives Marp does not have (see Kinds). slides expand replaces them with the directives they stand for, so the expanded deck is plain Marp. Outputs. HTML, PNG, JPEG and PDF, through Go libraries rather than a headless browser (see Command line for the known limits). PPTX is planned.

data: The deck is a Go text/template, evaluated before the Markdown is parsed. Everything the Go template language has — actions, pipelines, if, range, with, variables — works in a deck.
data.code-is-left-alone#Code is left alone: Fenced code blocks and inline code spans are set aside before the template runs and restored verbatim, so a slide about Go templates can show {{ .Name }} without escaping it.
data.data#Data:
The template’s dot holds the front matter’s keys, then the keys of its data: mapping, then the data given on the command line or in slides.yaml — each overriding the one before.
--- marp: true title: Quarterly review data: team: Platform --- # {{ .title }} Presented by the {{ .team }} team. From the command line:
Flag Gives --data file.yaml a YAML or JSON file of data (repeatable) --set key=value one value (repeatable)
data.generating-slides#Generating slides:
The whole body is one template, so a range that writes --- writes slides:
{{ range .releases }} --- # {{ .version }} {{ range .changes }}- {{ . }} {{ end }} {{ end }}
data.include#Include: {{ include "parts/agenda.md" }} inserts another file, relative to the deck.
data.page-and-total#Page and total: {{ page }} and {{ total }} are the slide’s number and the number of slides. They are known only once the deck has been split, so they are filled in then — a generated deck counts the slides it generated.
data.turning-it-off#Turning it off: --no-template reads the deck as plain Marp: {{ is text.
